evidence.note: Agent begins by listing /app, task configs, datasets, and reading run_eval.py to understand structural checks and the config schema (name/type/dataset_path/params) before coding — genuine orientation, not assuming a schema.

Inspects representative dataset files per type and confirms row/field schemas: classification train/test jsonl with text/label, STS/pair test.jsonl sentence1/sentence2, retrieval corpus/qrels/queries. Notes clustering/summarization output was truncated and plans to inspect those plus 'all STS configs for min/max score' — targeted per-type schema confirmation.

Writes evaluate.py declaring 'we have enough schema detail,' covering all six task types. This is the transition from orientation to implementation; the survey stopped at representative-file level with no cataloguing of config overrides (ignore_identical_ids, samples_per_label, max_fraction) and no explicit note of the corpus title+text rule or hierarchical labels.

No MTEB leaderboard cross-reference appears anywhere; the entire remainder is terminal-recovery attempts, so no further reconciliation of computed scores against known all-MiniLM-L6-v2 numbers ever occurs — the hallmark of anchor 8 is absent.

reasoning: The agent inspected representative datasets and configs for each of the six task types, confirmed row/field schemas, and understood the run_eval structural-check contract before implementing — squarely matching the level-5 anchor. It stopped short of level 8: it did not systematically catalogue where configs override defaults, did not explicitly reconcile the spec's tricky conventions (title+text, ignore_identical_ids, bootstrap k, shuffle composition), and performed zero MTEB leaderboard cross-referencing to anchor expected outputs. Truncated clustering/summarization inspection and unconfirmed min/max_score keep it from exceeding 5.
